role.altitude: The history lecturer keeps advising students, talking with prospective students, deciding placements, designing research and choosing readings; arranging appointments, answering the same questions, checking prerequisites, filling standard grant sections and typing citations shrink.
skills_to_grow: Checking suggested titles against the catalogue
role.ambitious_version: A lecturer who spends advising and grant time on substance, not on forms and lists.

tasks.short: Let students book advising slots, confirm appointments, review progress, advise students on academic and vocational curricula and career issues, refer them on, and note the advice.

steps.what: Student books an advising slot on the booking page
Lecturer confirms advising appointments with students
Lecturer reviews the student's progress and programme options
Lecturer advises the student on academic and vocational curricula and career issues
Lecturer refers the student to career services, internships or archives
Lecturer notes the advice in the student record

tasks.design: Students book an advising slot on a booking page linked to the lecturer's calendar, which sends the confirmation, instead of agreeing times by mail. The student system shows credits against programme requirements and open electives on one page, so preparation is quick. Advising and referring stay personal; no software recommends a path.
tasks.previous_blocker: Times were agreed by mail and transcripts compared by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Booking pages and degree progress views.
tasks.still_hard: Students combining programmes or studying abroad.
tasks.human_edge: Showing a history student where their skills are valued.

reach.learn: Whether referred students arrive better prepared.

evidence.claim: AI that steers students' education or evaluates learning is high-risk, so no software recommends a path here.

assumptions: Boundary: advising on curricula and careers; office hours (task 6364) and student records (task 6362) are sibling tasks.
s6 is the first record of the advice in the student record and keeps its full time.
Students' booking time is shown in s1 and is about what a mail took.
Advising and referring keep their full time.
unknowns: Whether the student system has a degree progress view.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few advising meetings; high: many students per term.

tasks.short: Prepare and present at open days, answer prospective students' questions, check course registration and prerequisites, decide placements, and coordinate placement activities with hosts.

steps.what: Lecturer prepares open day talks and programme information
Lecturer takes part in student recruitment at open days and talks with prospective students
Prospective student reads the programme questions page before mailing remaining questions
Lecturer answers prospective students' questions
Lecturer checks course registration and prerequisites
Lecturer decides student placements in internships or tracks
Lecturer coordinates placement activities with host organisations

tasks.design: A programme questions page answers common questions from the approved programme catalogue, so the lecturer answers only what it does not cover; no chat bot answers. The registration system checks prerequisites by rule and lists exceptions for the lecturer to decide. Host organisations post placements in a placement portal and the lecturer confirms there, instead of arranging each one by mail. Open days, talks and placement decisions stay with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Questions, prerequisite checks and placements were handled by mail and lists.
tasks.enabler_now: Questions pages, rule-based registration checks and placement portals.
tasks.still_hard: International applicants with unusual prior education.
tasks.human_edge: Convincing a doubtful student that history leads somewhere.
tasks.altitude: Less mail and checking; people work stays.

evidence.claim: AI used for admission is a high-risk use, so prerequisite checks are rules and exceptions go to the lecturer.

assumptions: Boundary: recruitment, registration and placement; advising students (task 6367) and supervising internships (task 6374) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s5: prerequisite rules set in the registration system by the programme office.
Prospective students' reading time is shown in s3 and is short.
Open days and placement decisions keep their full time.
research_questions: Do fewer registration errors reach the start of term?

incremental.description: Lecturer keeps the questions page current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few registrations and placements; high: large intake and many placements.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find the call, develop the research design, write the narrative, complete standard sections and the budget, collect partner letters, approve and submit grant proposals for external research funding.

steps.what: Lecturer finds funding calls and reads their requirements
Lecturer develops the research idea and design
Lecturer writes the scientific narrative of the grant proposal
Lecturer completes standard sections: CV, publications, data management plan and institutional statements
Lecturer prepares the budget
Lecturer collects partner letters and signatures
Lecturer checks and approves the final proposal
Lecturer submits the proposal in the funder's portal

approvals.approved_version: The full proposal with narrative, standard sections, budget and letters as approved by the lecturer in s7, for the call named in it; any change needs a new check before submitting.

tasks.design: A funding alert service lists calls on the lecturer's topics with deadlines and requirements, instead of searching funder sites. CVs, publication lists and institutional statements come from the research information system and the grants office templates. The budget template computes salary costs and overhead from the institution's rates. Partner letters are collected through electronic signature. The research design and narrative stay with the lecturer and are not uploaded to outside drafting tools.
tasks.previous_blocker: Standard sections and budgets were rebuilt for each call.
tasks.enabler_now: Funding alerts, research information systems and grants office templates.
tasks.human_edge: Arguing why this history matters now.
tasks.altitude: Less form filling; the argument stays.

reach.learn: Whether proposals reach the office earlier.

evidence.claim: A national research funder forbids referees to use generative AI and treats uploading a proposal as a confidentiality breach.

assumptions: Boundary: grant proposals; conducting research and publishing (task 6365) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s4: publication lists kept in the research information system, and templates from the grants office.
Input contract for s5: salary scales and overhead rates set in the budget template by the grants office.
Designing, writing the narrative, approving and submitting keep their full time.
research_questions: Are proposals submitted earlier before deadlines?

incremental.description: Lecturer keeps the publication list in the research system current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one large proposal; high: several smaller proposals per year.

tasks.short: Decide topics and level, search catalogues and databases, select specialized materials, format the bibliographies for outside reading assignments, and check availability in the library.

steps.what: Lecturer decides the topics and level for outside reading assignments
Lecturer searches catalogues and databases for specialized materials

loop.input: The topics and level, and the library catalogue and literature databases.
loop.check: Each title must resolve in the catalogue or by identifier; any title that does not resolve is dropped.
loop.stop: The lecturer searches by hand when suggestions miss known key works.
loop.why_not_simpler: Specialized materials are spread over many catalogues.

steps.what: Lecturer selects the materials for the list
Lecturer formats the citations and compiles the bibliographies
Lecturer checks availability and links in the library

tasks.design: A search step suggests titles from the catalogue and literature databases for the topics and level, and every title must resolve in the catalogue or by identifier, or it is dropped. Selecting stays with the lecturer. The reference manager imports citation data by identifier and formats the list in the required style, and the library's reading list tool shows availability and links per title.
tasks.previous_blocker: Citations were typed and availability checked one title at a time.
tasks.enabler_now: Reference managers, reading list tools and catalogue-checked suggestions.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a book that changes how students see a period.
tasks.altitude: Less typing and searching; choosing stays.

reach.learn: Whether missing titles are flagged before term.

evidence.claim: A literature database gives topic summaries and foundational papers.
Invented references pass plagiarism checks unflagged, so every title must resolve in the catalogue.

assumptions: Boundary: bibliographies for outside reading; selecting textbooks (task 6366) and preparing course materials (task 6358) are sibling tasks.
Deciding and selecting keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of specialized materials indexed in catalogues.
research_questions: Are reading lists ready earlier before term?

incremental.description: Lecturer reports catalogue gaps to the library.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: archival materials; high: well-catalogued published works.
